meaning: Cbuf = 0.0 sets the buffer compartment's compliance to zero, disabling the spinal buffering branch (Racc and Rbuf remain defined but inert). The default model therefore runs with no compliant buffer storage.

could_move.what: States using the buffer term stay on the no-buffer path
Second buffer reference; a nonzero Cbuf would change this term's scaling or division
Downstream buffer use is effectively dead code with this default
Spinal buffering entry point runs with a disabled branch unless it overrides Cbuf
m5-vs-m6 comparison may credit model differences that are really the disabled buffer

expectation: Unknown in size. Direction: a nonzero Cbuf adds compliance, so expect damped/slower pressure transients; with 0.0 the traces are the stiff no-buffer case. I cannot tell whether the fitted parameters absorbed the missing buffer.

check.why: Lists every use and override of Cbuf cheaply, showing whether any entry point re-enables the branch before anything is re-fit.
